question: Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by July 31?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.
research:
I couldn't open the IMF PortWatch page, so I can't give you the latest official 7-day average. The proxy also blocked every page I tried to fetch, so everything below comes from search-result summaries. Up to 16 July, traffic was around 30 ships a day, about three times the 10-a-day threshold. I found nothing published by 16 July that settles the question.

## 1. Resolution source
- **Latest PortWatch value:** not found. The connection to the PortWatch page was refused, and I couldn't open Statista's mirror of the "transit calls" series either. [PortWatch](https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c), [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1622216/mea-bab-el-mandeb-strait-transit-calls/)
- **Closest proxy, May 2026:** Wikipedia, which may be quoting PortWatch-style counts, says the strait carried about 31 ships a day. That level had held since January 2024; before the Gaza war it was about 75 a day. [Wikipedia, Red Sea crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea_crisis)

## 2. Current status
- **2026-07-16:** Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. The last levels I found are roughly 3 times the threshold, and I found no published 7-day average at or below 10.
- **Unconfirmed:** a third-party source says PortWatch's "transit calls" rose a little in the first half of 2026. [Red Team Analysis](https://redanalysis.org/2026/10/08/houthis-bab-el-mandeb-maritime-transport/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first, on or before 16 July)
- **2026-07-13:** The Houthis restarted attacks on Saudi Arabia, which raises the risk to Saudi-linked shipping in the strait. [Wikipedia, Red Sea crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea_crisis)
- **March to mid-July 2026:** Iran closed Hormuz during the US-Iran war, and Saudi Arabia shifted its exports to the Red Sea:
  - Saudi crude shipped through Bab al-Mandab was about 8 times the same period of 2025. [Wikipedia, Bab al-Mandab Strait crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bab_al-Mandab_Strait_crisis)
  - Kpler puts Yanbu crude loadings at about 3.5 to 3.8 million barrels a day. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/policy/international/5991796-houthi-saudi-arabia-attacks-bab-el-mandeb-strait/), [gCaptain](https://gcaptain.com/saudis-yanbu-port-bustles-as-more-tankers-cross-chokepoint-dark/)
- **During the Iran war:** The Houthis have repeatedly threatened to close the strait, including if Gulf states join the US-Israel war on Iran. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/22/houthis-red-sea-bab-el-mandeb-saudi-oil-iran.html), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/world/bab-el-mandeb-strait-faces-growing-threat-houthi-attacks-raise-fears-second-hormuz)
- **Undated:** A US MARAD advisory said the Houthis had not attacked commercial ships since the Gaza ceasefire in October 2025. [MARAD 2026-006](https://www.maritime.dot.gov/msci/2026-006-red-sea-bab-el-mandeb-strait-gulf-aden-arabian-sea-and-somali-basin-houthi-attacks)

## 4. Base rates
- **2024-2025 crisis:** At the worst of the Houthi campaign, daily transits were still about 25 to 31. S&P counted an average of 28 a day in the week to 2025-07-06, against more than 70 before the war. [S&P Global](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/shipping/070925-factbox-red-sea-transits-in-renewed-focus-following-houthis-first-attacks-in-2025)
- **Has the 7-day average ever been at or below 10?** I found no record of it since November 2023. In my own records (not a sourced figure), PortWatch's low point in 2024 was in the high teens to low 20s.
- **What it would take:** Getting to 10 or below would need roughly a 65 to 70% fall from the mid-2026 level of about 30 a day, held for a whole week.
- **Why it's hard to reach:** Even during attack waves, container ships, bulk carriers and non-Saudi or non-Western ships have kept sailing. PortWatch's AIS-based counts can also be pushed down when ships switch off their transponders, which happens more during attacks.

## 5. Other forecasts
- **Polymarket:** runs a ladder of contracts called "Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by...?". I couldn't load it to get the price as of 16 July. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-closed-by)
- **Related markets:** from about 2026-07-13 there were also markets on the average daily Bab el-Mandeb transits on July 31, with bands such as 28-30 and 34-36. The bands people were trading suggest they expected around 30 a day, not something near 10. [Orrery mirror](https://orrery.me/markets/will-there-be-between-28-and-30-average-daily-transits-of-the-bab-el-mandeb-strait-on-july-31-20260713195907054)
- **Kalshi, Manifold and expert forecasts:** none found.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Houthi escalation:** a formal blockade, or attacks on ships in general rather than only Saudi-linked ones, would be the main way to a Yes. That risk is heightened after the attacks restarted on 13 July.
- **US-Iran war:** if Gulf states join the war, the Houthis have threatened to shut the strait completely.
- **Naval response:** EU (Aspides) or US convoy or strike operations could keep traffic moving.
- **Data timing:** PortWatch updates with a lag of several days. The data for July 31 may arrive in early August, and the rules allow until 14 August.
- **Key gap:** I couldn't confirm the 7-day average on PortWatch itself. It should be checked directly before relying on the levels above.

the counts could understate real traffic.
- **For No:**
  - Traffic was steady at about 31 a day as of May 2026.
  - Markets created around 13 July traded July 31 transit bands near 28 to 36, not near 10.
  - MARAD reported no Houthi attacks on commercial ships since the October 2025 ceasefire.
  - Even at the 2024 peak, container, bulk and non-Western ships kept transiting.
  - Coverage that appears to postdate the forecast date, such as CNBC on 22 July, still describes threats rather than a closure.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** The Houthis strike Saudi targets and a few Saudi-linked tankers. Some Western operators hold off, but Chinese and other traffic continues. The 7-day average dips to the mid-20s and stays there through 31 July.
- **Yes:** Gulf states formally join the war. The Houthis declare a total blockade and hit several ships of various flags within days. Insurers withdraw cover, ships go dark, and AIS-counted transits collapse below 10 for a week before late July. A PortWatch data glitch producing a spuriously low value is a smaller additional path.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** I start at about 1.5%. I move up to about 3% because of the live escalation on 13 July, the extraordinary context of the Iran war, and the small chance of AIS or data artifacts. I don't go higher because the drop needed is huge (about 70%, sustained for a week), the time is short, nothing like it happened even in 2024, and the markets expected around 30.

Probability: 3%
